summary:
Outpost Command 3D: Artemis & Ares Mission Simulator is a space exploration and survival game that introduces players to the challenges of becoming astronauts and managing a space outpost. Players can choose the Moon (Artemis) or Mars (Ares) mission.

The main objective is to manage the outpost throughout a five-day mission. Players must complete daily activities, earn science points, and keep the astronaut crew safe. They can explore areas, operate solar panels, manage electricity, maintain oxygen supplies, protect the crew from radiation, and grow plants in a hydroponic garden. They also complete challenges, including the Outpost XOX game and NASA science activities.

During the mission, players face solar flares, dust storms, power failures, and rival robots. They must make decisions to balance limited resources, including oxygen, food, battery power, health, and radiation shielding.

The game features NASA photographs, scientific information, and space research concepts, helping players understand the difficulties of living and working beyond Earth.

To succeed, players must complete all five daily objectives, keep systems operating, and protect the crew. Successful completion allows them to graduate as a NASA Junior Flight Director. By combining exploration, resource management, problem-solving, and science education, the game offers an introduction to space survival.
details:
1. HOW IT FUNCTIONS?

Step 1: Choose one of two space missions:

  • Artemis: Explore and manage an outpost on the Moon.
  • Ares: Explore and manage an outpost on Mars.
  • Then, choose Guided Adventure to learn the controls and receive instructions, or start the Five-Day Mission directly.

Step 2: Follow the Steps in Cadet Step 1-6:

A: Enter the Central Outpost
Use WASD or Arrow Keys to walk north through the South Airlock and enter the Central Outpost.

B: Learn to Manage Power
Follow the instruction and select a power mode: ECO, NORM or BOOST. Learn to balance electricity supply and demand.

C: Grow Space Flowers
Open FLOWER GARDEN at the Hydroponic Dome. Click the plant pods to grow and bloom space flowers.

D: Play the Oxygen XOX Game
Open O₂ XOX GAME at the O₂ & Power Bunker. Play the 3×3 game against Astro-Bot.

E: Protect the Crew from Radiation
Follow the instruction to set WEST SHELTER to BOOST or open the SHIELD CONSOLE to strengthen radiation protection.

F: Complete Cadet Training
Click FINISH & GRADUATE when instructed. Then press MENU to begin the full Five-Day Mission.


Step 3: Play the 5-day mission

After completing Cadet Training, players can begin the full Five-Day Mission. Each day has a different NASA-inspired activity. Follow the instructions on the screen, complete the daily objective, and keep the astronauts alive!

DAY 1: Solar Array & Power Budgeting

Picture shows the instruction user have to fulfil that day.
  1. Click OPEN SOLAR ALIGNMENT.
  2. Align all three solar wings towards the Sun.

3. Adjust the power modes (ECO, NORM or BOOST) to balance electricity supply and demand.4. Choose your end-of-day power management decision.

DAY 2: Oxygen Life Support ⭕❌

Click PLAY O₂ XOX CONSOLE.

  1. Play the 3×3 XOX game against Astro-Bot.
  2. Connect three life-support subsystems to stabilise oxygen.
  3. Choose how to manage oxygen reserves and power.

DAY 3: Radiation Protection 🛡️

  1. Respond to the incoming solar flare warning.
  2. Click OPEN STORM SHIELD CONSOLE.
  3. Reinforce the West Storm Shelter using the available protection systems.
  4. Choose whether to boost the magnetic shield or conserve battery power.

DAY 4: Space Garden 🌻

  1. Click OPEN CLICK-TO-FLOWER GARDEN.
  2. Click the plant pods to grow flowers.
  3. Develop the plants through Seed → Sprout → Bud → Bloom.
  4. Harvest the flowers to increase food and oxygen supplies.

DAY 5: Communication & NASA Science 📡

  1. Click OPEN COMMS & OSDR LAB.
  2. Test the radio communication delay between the outpost and Earth.
  3. Run a NASA OSDR biology study.
  4. Make decisions during the communication delay and micrometeorite emergency.

Complete all five daily activities, manage your resources wisely, and protect your astronaut crew. At the end of Day 5, receive your mission debrief and final score!

2. What does the project do and how does it work?

Our project is an interactive 3D space exploration and survival game where players experience life as astronauts managing an outpost on the Moon or Mars. Players complete a five-day mission involving solar panel alignment, electricity management, oxygen production, radiation protection, hydroponic gardening, and NASA science activities. They explore the outpost, operate equipment, collect science points, and make decisions to keep the crew alive.

3. What are the benefits?

The game makes learning about space science more interesting and interactive. It develops problem-solving, critical thinking, decision-making, and resource-management skills. Players also gain a better understanding of renewable energy, life-support systems, radiation, plant growth, and space exploration. It also increases understanding of Lunar and Martial.

4. What is the intended impact?

We hope to inspire 7-12 year old students to become more interested in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). The project aims to increase awareness of the challenges astronauts face and encourage young people to explore future careers in space science and engineering, especially the understanding of Lunar and Martial.

5. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

The game was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Three.js was used to create the interactive 3D environment, while Tailwind CSS helped design the interface. NASA photographs and space-related datasets were incorporated to support scientific learning. The game runs in a web browser and does not require specialised hardware.

6. How is the project creative?

The project combines a 3D exploration experience with survival challenges, educational activities, and realistic space-related scenarios. Players can choose between two destinations, explore different habitat areas, interact with rival robots, drive a rover, play mini-games, and manage resources. This turns science lessons into an engaging mission-based experience.

7. What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered educational value, scientific accuracy, gameplay, user-friendliness, and accessibility. We also considered the limited resources available in space, different environmental conditions on the Moon and Mars, possible mission hazards, and astronaut safety. The game was designed to be engaging while ensuring that players learn meaningful scientific concepts.
